title: Konark Sun Temple in the Brahma Purana and Ratha Saptami Puja
desc: What the Brahma Purana says about Kona-Aditya (Konark), the Sun temple on the Odisha coast, and the simple Ratha Saptami sun worship it describes.
alt: Sun rising over the sea near the Konark Sun temple in Odisha, Ratha Saptami worship
caption: The Sun, worshipped as Kona-Aditya on the Odisha coast.
intro: Most people know Konark through its stone chariot wheels. The **Brahma Purana** knows it by an older name, **Kona-Aditya**, the Sun god of the corner, and describes it as one of the most rewarding shrines on the Odisha coast. It also gives a simple **Ratha Saptami puja** that anyone can follow.
takeaways: The Purana calls the shrine **Kona-Aditya** and says seeing the deity burns away sins.
**Ratha Saptami** is the bright seventh (Shukla Saptami) of **Magha** month.
The rite needs only a **copper vessel, red flowers, sesame and rice**, and a sea or river bath at dawn.
The text offers **pongal cooked with jaggery** to the Sun.

p: The Purana opens with the country of **Odra** (Odisha), on the southern sea coast, running up to the limits of the Viraja region. It calls it a **land of liberation**, where learned people keep their rites carefully and every community is devoted to dharma.
Here the Sun is worshipped as **Kona-Aditya**. The temple precinct is said to span **half a yojana**. The text says that seeing the deity is enough to burn away sins.

sections.h: The day to go: Ratha Saptami
p: **Magha month** is dear to the Sun. On the bright seventh, **Ratha Saptami**, the devotee rises before dawn and bathes in the sea near the temple. He offers water to the gods, sages and ancestors, and puts on white clothes.

sections.h: The simple Sun worship, step by step
ol: Sit on the shore and draw an **eight-petal lotus** with a red centre.
Put **red sandalwood, sesame, rice, red flowers and darbha grass** in a copper vessel with water, and cover it with a second vessel.
Meditate on the Sun as a calm, two-armed form in red, with a halo of light, giving blessings.
Lift the vessel to the head and offer the **arghya** with the three-syllable mantra. Anyone not initiated may simply say **"Om Suryaya namah, tarpayami"**.
Worship at the points of the lotus, offer **pongal cooked with jaggery**, and chant the Sun mantra as many times as you can.

p: The Purana promises **long life, health and prosperity**. Visiting the temple with three circumambulations and red flowers is said to equal ten horse sacrifices. It also names the sleeping and awakening Ekadashis, solar transit days, and a Saptami that falls on a Sunday as good days to visit.

sections.h: A second shrine on the same shore
p: On the same shore stands a Shiva temple called **Rameshwara**, which the text says gives the merit of the Rajasuya sacrifice.

If you cannot reach Odisha, a simple Sun offering at home on **Ratha Saptami morning** follows the spirit of this text: an early bath, water offered to the rising Sun, and jaggery pongal as the offering.

faq.a: It is the **Shukla Saptami (bright seventh) of Magha month**, dear to the Sun god, when the Brahma Purana advises a dawn bath and Sun worship.
It is the Brahma Purana's name for the Sun shrine on the Odisha coast, now known as **Konark**.

faq.q: What should be offered to the Sun on Ratha Saptami?
faq.a: The text names **red flowers, red sandalwood, sesame, rice and darbha grass** for the arghya, and **pongal cooked with jaggery** as the food offering.

note: This is a retelling in our own words. Rituals should be followed according to your family tradition and local priest's guidance.
